doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: First gig with McDonald and studio versus touring players
summary: Prep, rehearsals at the Power Plant, the loud first gig at Del Mar with bandmates named, and why producers use their own studio players.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: So you did some rehearsing with him or did you just like do gigs?

No, we had, I think we had, well I got a cassette of a live show so I went to the woodshed with that. And then I think we had two or three days of rehearsal with the full band out at a place called The Power Plant, which was a big rehearsal facility. And the first gig I did with him was at the Delmar Racetrack down towards San Diego. And I’ve got to say, man, it was a night I will never forget. A) I’ve never played — up to that point I don’t think I’d played in a band that was quite that loud. But it was super musical. David Pack from Ambrosia was the guitar player at the time, and Vince Denham was our woodwind player, Scott Plunkett was playing keyboards, my good friend George Perilli who we ended up playing for years. He was from Pittsburgh. Great drummer. And a guy that grew up with Mike in St. Louis, Chuck Sabatino, who has since passed — the only guy to this day who can go toe to toe vocally with Michael. And he was in the band so it was fantastic. It was great. It was a fun night, the first night of almost 20 years of nights.
Now do those type of guys use different players in the studio than they do live?

Yeah. Usually. Although I did some session work with Mike but normally that call — it seems like it comes down to the producer, and the producer calls his guys, and I think Ted Templeman was producing Mike at that point. And I’ve got to say though, that was a little bit of a tough pill to swallow, only because I felt like certainly the guys in the touring band were capable of recording, but I don’t think it was really Mike’s call because the producers control the money and — but Mike was kind of, we got in there on a few tunes that’s documented. That’s great.
